ambiguities.evidence: Section 4 separately introduces x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1 as convenient definitions, and Lemma 4.2's proof does not separately discuss h_1. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, algorithm and initialization; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]
ambiguities.impact: A formal rendering must treat m=0 as the artificial base case, not as an additional computed refinement step.
ambiguities.issue: The algorithmic display defines ordinary refinement updates for m>=1, whereas Lemma 4.2 also quantifies m=0.

ambiguities.evidence: The source supplies only the abstract componentwise relation |h_{m+1}| <= u|x_m-d_m| and the standing assumption that operations are well-defined. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof; PDF p. 3/printed 818, floating-point model]
ambiguities.impact: The source contract requires the stated h_{m+1} bound, not a stronger machine-specific rounding semantics.
ambiguities.issue: The paper does not specify an IEEE rounding mode or detailed treatment of underflow for the final subtraction.

contract_plain_english: For every refinement index m>=0, the computed next iterate differs componentwise from the exact solution by at most (1+u) times the absolute inverse applied to the exact intermediate residual, plus u times the magnitude of the exact solution. This is an explicit forward-error bound for the rounded update and contains no norm or big-O term. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second inequality and proof]

source_evidence.observation: The problem is Ax=b with n equations and n unknowns over a floating-point subset of the reals. Unit roundoff u is positive, nu <= .01, every floating-point operation mentioned is assumed well-defined, and absolute values and inequalities are componentwise.
The exact solution is x=A^{-1}b, so A is implicitly nonsingular; Gaussian elimination uses column pivoting.

The initial computed solution x_1 and corrections d_m are obtained by column-pivoted solves; x_{m+1} is the floating-point subtraction of d_m from x_m. The artificial initialization is x_0=0, r_0=-b, d_0=-x_1. Both single- and double-precision residual accumulation are considered.

source_evidence.observation: q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b is defined as the exact residual of the unrounded corrected value x_m-d_m.

statement.algorithm_linkage: This is specifically the second part of Lemma 4.2. It bounds the componentwise forward error of the next computed iterate using the exact intermediate residual q_{m+1} and the rounding error of the final subtraction; it does not itself assert convergence, backward stability, or a normwise estimate. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 and proof]
binders: n is the number of equations and unknowns; A is an n-by-n real matrix, b and x are n-vectors, and x=A^{-1}b. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 opening; PDF p. 8/printed 823, Section 3 basic-result paragraph]
m ranges over 0,1,2,... in the displayed claim. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
u is the positive single-precision relative-roundoff bound. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
conclusions: Componentwise, |x_{m+1}-x| <= (1+u)|A^{-1}||q_{m+1}| + u|x|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second displayed inequality]
constants_and_indexing: The coefficients are exactly 1+u and u; there is no anonymous C_i factor in this inequality. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second inequality]
The offset is q_{m+1} to x_{m+1}, with m beginning at 0. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
The m=0 case uses x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1 rather than a normal refinement correction. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, convenient initialization]
definitions_and_conventions: q_{m+1}=A(x_m-d_m)-b=A(x_m-d_m-x) is exact, even though x_m and d_m are computed quantities. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, definition before Lemma 4.1; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]

Vertical bars denote entrywise absolute value and every displayed vector inequality is componentwise. Products such as |A^{-1}||q_{m+1}| are ordinary matrix-vector products of nonnegative entries. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 componentwise convention]
The proof uses x_m-d_m=A^{-1}q_{m+1}+x, followed by the rounded update. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]
error_notions: |x_{m+1}-x| is a componentwise forward error between a computed iterate and the exact solution. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second inequality]

|q_{m+1}| is the componentwise magnitude of an exact residual associated with the unrounded corrected value, not the computed residual r_m. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition; PDF p. 9/printed 824, r_m definition]
exceptional_values: A^{-1} requires A to be nonsingular. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, x=A^{-1}b context]

Floating-point overflow, undefined operations, and non-real exceptional values are outside the model because every cited result is assumed well-defined in a floating-point subset of the reals. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
No nonzero-component assumption on x or q_{m+1} is imposed by Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
higher_order_terms: The displayed result is a finite explicit inequality with no O(u^2), asymptotic remainder, or omitted higher-order term. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 second inequality]
hypotheses: A is nonsingular, inherited from the use of A^{-1} and x=A^{-1}b rather than restated in Lemma 4.2. [PDF p. 8/printed 823, Section 3 basic-result paragraph]
x_m and d_m belong to the column-pivoted iterative-refinement process, with x_0=0 and d_0=-x_1 for the m=0 extension. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm definition]
The computed update has the componentwise rounding representation x_{m+1}=x_m-d_m+h_{m+1}, |h_{m+1}| <= u|x_m-d_m|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]
All referenced floating-point operations are well-defined. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
Lemma 4.2 states no additional condition involving kappa(A^{-1}) or the anonymous C_i constants. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
implicit_context: The result belongs to Section 4's analysis of iterative refinement following Gaussian elimination with column pivoting. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm definition]

The paper studies both s.p.r.a. and d.p.r.a.; this inequality does not involve the residual-precision parameter and therefore is common to both variants. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 precision paragraph; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
For m=0, the convenient definitions give q_1=Ax_1-b, so the bound includes the initially computed solution. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, initialization; PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition]
norms: No vector or matrix norm occurs in the conclusion; replacing the componentwise inequality by a norm inequality would be a different claim. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2; PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention]
numerical_model: Single-precision floating-point arithmetic has relative-roundoff bound u, with nu <= .01 and well-defined results assumed. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, Section 2 floating-point model]
The only rounding step used explicitly in this proof is the final vector subtraction, represented by |h_{m+1}| <= u|x_m-d_m|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2 proof]

Residual accumulation may be single precision or double precision followed by conversion to single precision, but that distinction does not occur in this bound. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 precision paragraph; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]

undebatable_constraints: The quantified range is every integer m >= 0. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
The conclusion is componentwise, not normwise. [PDF p. 3/printed 818, componentwise convention; PDF p. 11/printed 826, Lemma 4.2]
The left side is the forward error |x_{m+1}-x|, not a residual or backward error. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, second displayed inequality]
q_{m+1} is the exact residual of x_m-d_m, while x_{m+1} is the rounded update. [PDF p. 10/printed 825, q-definition; PDF p. 11/printed 826, proof]
The term multiplying |A^{-1}||q_{m+1}| is exactly 1+u, and the additive data term is exactly u|x|. [PDF p. 11/printed 826, second displayed inequality]
The result is inherited from the column-pivoted iterative-refinement algorithm and applies to both residual-accumulation variants. [PDF p. 9/printed 824, Section 4 algorithm and precision paragraph]
